stories.title: Passengers stranded as strike disrupts flights at Kenya's main airport
stories.summary: Hundreds of passengers were stranded at Kenya's main airport in the capital, Nairobi, as flight disruptions continued for the second day amid a workers' strike. Jomo Kenyatta International Airport (JKIA) is a key regional transport hub. On Sunday, the airports authority and the national carrier, Kenya Airways, warned departing flights may be delayed. A new round of talks between unions and airport managers was due to take place on Monday, although discussions broke up a day earlier without agreement. Aviation sector workers are on a nationwide go-slow strike to demand better working conditions and the implementation of a previously agreed deal. Those hoping to get on a flight have been stuck at JKIA, with some spending the night in and around the check-in areas waiting for news. Kenya Airways said in its latest update that due to "the industrial action by air traffic control workers", it is experiencing delays of more than six hours, and the flight backlog has forced it to cancel some departures. It has apologised for the disruption and said passengers who would like to change or reschedule their flights could do so without a penalty. Flight tracking website Flightradar24 showed a host of delayed, cancelled or diverted flights. RwandAir said on Monday that it had cancelled two flights due to the ongoing "operational constraints affecting air traffic control services" at the airport. This followed earlier cancellations on Sunday. Mendel Goldman, who was travelling to a wedding in Florida, told the Reuters news agency that his flight had been cancelled, after several delays.

stories.title: Chinese Vice Premier Ding Xuexiang to take part in EEF on September 2-4 — MFA
stories.summary: BEIJING, August 31. Vice Premier of the State Council of the People’s Republic of China Ding Xuexiang will travel to Russia to attend the 11th Eastern Economic Forum (EEF) on September 2-4, China’s Foreign Ministry reported. "At the invitation of the government of the Russian Federation, from September 2 to 4, Member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and Vice Premier of the State Council Ding Xuexiang will travel to Russia to attend the 11th Eastern Economic Forum," the report said. He will also participate in the 13th meeting of the China-Russia Investment Cooperation Committee, the 23rd meeting of the China-Russia Energy Cooperation Committee, and the 8th China-Russia Energy Business Forum, the ministry added. Russian Presidential Aide Yury Ushakov said earlier that Chinese Vice Premier Ding Xuexiang would take part in the EEF plenary session together with Russian President Vladimir Putin. The Eastern Economic Forum will be held September 1-4 in Vladivostok on the campus of the Far Eastern Federal University. The main theme of this year’s EEF is "The Far East: Development for the Benefit of People." The event is organized by the Roscongress Foundation with the support of the Russian government. TASS is its general information partner.
